440	
441	# SSA construction, DCE, then a final SSA canonicalization (clone +
442	# deterministic renumbering), which makes the emitted IR the fixed point of
443	# the whole sequence: DCE may leave numbering holes, and the trailing ssa
444	# pass compacts them without changing structure or semantics.
445	DEFAULT_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa")
446	
447	# Legal alternatives: extra early normalization, an explicit DCE fixpoint
448	# repeat, and an ssa/dce interleaving -- all end in the canonicalizing ssa
449	# pass, so each is a fixed point of its own sequence.
450	ALT_DOUBLE_SSA = ("ssa", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
451	ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "dce", "dce", "ssa")
452	ALT_INTERLEAVE = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
453	# Legal but less optimizing: construction + canonicalization only.
454	NO_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa",)
455	# The README-documented core without the trailing canonicalization: legal,
456	# used for cross-order semantics and determinism (its endpoint may carry
457	# numbering holes and is compared on observables, not text).
458	RAW_CORE_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce")
459	
460	LEGAL_ORDERS = {
461	    "default ssa,dce,ssa": DEFAULT_ORDER,
462	    "alt ssa,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_DOUBLE_SSA,
463	    "alt ssa,dce,dce,ssa": ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT,
464	    "alt ssa,dce,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_INTERLEAVE,
465	    "no-dce ssa": NO_DCE_ORDER,
466	    "raw core ssa,dce": RAW_CORE_ORDER,
467	}
468	
469	# Orders whose endpoint is the canonical fixed point used by the strict
470	# idempotence test.
471	IDEMPOTENT_ORDERS = {
472	    name: order for name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items()
473	    if name != "raw core ssa,dce"
474	}

477	def apply_order(module: Module, order) -> Module:
478	    """Apply ``order`` (a tuple of pass names) to ``module``.
479	
480	    :raises ValueError: if a pass name is unknown, if instruction selection
481	        appears anywhere but the end, or if ``dce`` is scheduled before the
482	        first ``ssa`` (DCE requires an SSA module).
483	    """
484	    ssa_seen = bool(getattr(module, "ssa", False))
485	    for index, name in enumerate(order):
486	        if name == "ssa":
487	            module = to_ssa(module)
488	            ssa_seen = True
489	        elif name == "dce":
490	            if not ssa_seen:
491	                raise ValueError(
492	                    "pass order violates precondition: 'dce' requires an SSA "
493	                    "module, but no 'ssa' pass precedes it"
494	                )
495	            module = eliminate_dead_code(module)
496	        elif name == "isel":
497	            raise ValueError(
498	                "pass order violates stage contract: instruction selection "
499	                "('isel') must be the final stage"
500	            )
501	        else:
502	            raise ValueError(f"unknown pass in order: {name!r}")
503	    return module
504	
505	
506	def compile_ast(ast: dict, order):
507	    """Compile a fresh copy of ``ast`` through lowering and ``order``.
508	
509	    Returns ``(unoptimized_module, optimized_module, target_text)`` where
510	    the target text is instruction selection (rendering) run last.
511	    """
512	    lowered = lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast))
513	    optimized = apply_order(lowered, order)
514	    return lowered, optimized, render_module(optimized)

517	def structural_signature(module: Module):
518	    """Numbering-independent structural fingerprint of a module."""
519	    signature = []
520	    for fn_ in module.functions:
521	        blocks = []
522	        for block in fn_.blocks:
523	            instructions = []
524	            for ins in block.instructions:
525	                if isinstance(ins, Const):
526	                    instructions.append(("const", ins.value))
527	                elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
528	                    instructions.append(("copy",))
529	                elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
530	                    instructions.append((ins.kind, ins.operator))
531	                elif isinstance(ins, Call):
532	                    instructions.append(("call", ins.name, len(ins.args)))
533	            terminator = type(block.terminator).__name__
534	            blocks.append((
535	                block.id, terminator, len(block.phis),
536	                tuple(instructions),
537	            ))
538	        signature.append((
539	            fn_.name, fn_.ret_type,
540	            tuple((p.name, p.temp.type if p.temp is not None
541	                   else p.slot.type) for p in fn_.params),
542	            tuple(blocks),
543	        ))
544	    return tuple(signature)

552	def _emit_function(name="emit"):
553	    return func(name, [param("v", "int")], "int", [ret(var("v"))])

556	# A) Constants and phi propagation at a branch convergence.
557	#
558	# `a` is the same dominating constant on BOTH outgoing edges, so its merge
559	# phi is trivial (one incoming SSA value) and is pruned during SSA
560	# construction; the returned value is that constant propagated through the
561	# join.  `b` carries genuinely different values per edge and needs a real
562	# merge phi consumed by a side-effecting call.
563	def _join_program():
564	    return program(
565	        func("join", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
566	            let("k", "int", int_(7)),
567	            let("a", "int", int_(0)),
568	            if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("k"))],
569	                 [assign("a", var("k"))]),
570	            let("b", "int", int_(0)),
571	            if_(var("c"),
572	                [assign("b", arith("add", var("x"), int_(1)))],
573	                [assign("b", arith("sub", var("x"), int_(1)))]),
574	            let("s", "int", call("emit", [var("b")])),
575	            ret(arith("add", var("a"), var("s"))),
576	        ]),
577	        _emit_function(),
578	    )
579	
580	
581	# B) Deletable pure computations vs. still-side-effecting expressions.
582	#
583	# `d` and `junk` are pure chains nobody consumes: DCE deletes them (and
584	# their constants), but BOTH calls remain roots even though `ignored`'s
585	# result is never read -- deleting either would drop observable output.
586	def _clean_program():
587	    return program(
588	        func("clean", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
589	            let("d", "int",
590	                arith("mul", arith("add", int_(1), int_(2)), int_(3))),
591	            let("keptarg", "int", arith("add", var("n"), int_(10))),
592	            let("v", "int", call("observe", [var("keptarg")])),
593	            let("ignored", "int", call("observe", [int_(99)])),
594	            let("junk", "int",
595	                arith("add", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(3)), var("d"))),
596	            ret(arith("add", var("v"), int_(4))),
597	        ]),
598	        _emit_function("observe"),
599	    )
600	
601	
602	# C) Loop-invariant value plus a conditional branch inside the loop.
603	#
604	# `base` is loop invariant and defined before the header; the loop still
605	# carries real header phis for `i` and `total`, and the in-loop if makes the
606	# side-effecting call happen only on iterations that take its else edge.
607	def _loop_program():
608	    return program(
609	        func("loopsum", [param("n", "int"), param("k", "int")], "int", [
610	            let("base", "int", arith("add", var("k"), int_(1))),
611	            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
612	            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
613	            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
614	                if_(compare("gt", var("i"), int_(1)),
615	                    [assign("total", arith(
616	                        "add",
617	                        arith("add", var("total"), var("base")),
618	                        var("i")))],
619	                    [
620	                        let("t", "int", call("ping", [var("i")])),
621	                        assign("total", arith("add", var("total"), var("t"))),
622	                    ]),
623	                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
624	            ]),
625	            ret(var("total")),
626	        ]),
627	        _emit_function("ping"),
628	    )
629	
630	
631	# D) An inlineable call with dead code introduced after it.
632	#
633	# `dbl` is a trivial inline candidate; no pass order actually inlines it, so
634	# every order keeps the call and its observable position.  The pure
635	# computations built AFTER the call (`junk1`, `junk2`) are dead and vanish
636	# under DCE, while the later side-effecting call `after` is preserved.
637	def _around_program():
638	    return program(
639	        func("around", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
640	            let("v", "int", call("dbl", [arith("add", var("n"), int_(1))])),
641	            let("junk1", "int", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(9))),
642	            let("junk2", "int", arith("add", var("junk1"), int_(5))),
643	            let("w", "int", call("after", [var("v")])),
644	            ret(var("v")),
645	        ]),
646	        func("dbl", [param("x", "int")], "int",
647	             [ret(arith("mul", var("x"), int_(2)))]),
648	        _emit_function("after"),
649	    )

652	# E1) Zero divisor on one arm of a branch; the other arm terminates fine.
653	def _guarded_fault_program():
654	    return program(
655	        func("guarded", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
656	            let("d", "int", int_(0)),
657	            if_(var("c"),
658	                [
659	                    let("e", "int", call("emit", [int_(1)])),
660	                    let("q", "int", arith("div", var("x"), var("d"))),
661	                    ret(arith("add", var("q"), var("e"))),
662	                ],
663	                [
664	                    let("e2", "int", call("emit", [int_(2)])),
665	                    ret(var("e2")),
666	                ]),
667	        ]),

669	    )

797	def _first_difference(expected: Outcome, actual: Outcome):
798	    """Name the first observable that differs, in comparison order."""
799	    if expected.kind != actual.kind:
800	        return "termination kind", expected.kind, actual.kind
801	    if expected.output != actual.output:
802	        return "standard output (ordered call trace)", expected.output, \
803	            actual.output
804	    if expected.kind == "fault":
805	        if expected.category != actual.category:
806	            return "runtime error category", expected.category, \
807	                actual.category
808	        if expected.site != actual.site:
809	            return "runtime error trigger site", expected.site, actual.site
810	        if expected.operands != actual.operands:
811	            return "runtime error operands", expected.operands, \
812	                actual.operands
813	    else:
814	        if expected.value != actual.value:
815	            return "return value", expected.value, actual.value
816	    return None

819	def _mismatch_message(label, order_name, entry, arguments, expected, actual):
820	    diff = _first_difference(expected, actual)
821	    header = (
822	        f"semantic mismatch for sample {label!r}, order {order_name!r}, "
823	        f"entry {entry!r}, arguments {arguments!r}"
824	    )
825	    if diff is None:
826	        return header
827	    field, wanted, got = diff
828	    return (
829	        f"{header}\n"
830	        f"first differing observable: {field}\n"
831	        f"  expected: {wanted!r}\n"
832	        f"  actual:   {got!r}\n"
833	        f"baseline outcome: {expected!r}\n"
834	        f"this order:       {actual!r}"
835	    )

"""Pass-ordering and idempotence semantic regression tests.

The existing suites pin each pass in isolation (lowering, non-SSA -> SSA,
SSA dead-code elimination) and compare non-SSA vs SSA behavior.  This module
instead treats the compiler as a *pipeline* made of the existing public
entry points and checks that:

1. One legal source program, fed through the existing entry point
   (:func:`lower_module`, which still runs AST validation, name resolution
   and type checking), produces the same observable behavior under the
   default optimization pipeline and every alternative *legal* pass order,
   using the unoptimized (non-SSA) result as the semantic baseline.
2. For fixed source, options and order, repeated compilations are
   byte-identical (determinism), while *different* orders are only required
   to agree on observable behavior -- never on instruction or text layout.
3. Re-applying the same pass sequence to an optimized result changes
   neither the canonicalized IR nor the emitted target text (idempotence);
   each repeatable pass is also a fixed point on its own.
4. Orderings may only permute passes inside the existing stage contracts:
   SSA construction precedes every SSA-dependent optimization, and
   instruction selection (here, the deterministic :func:`render_module`
   emission) runs after IR optimization.

Passes and preconditions (nothing new is added to the compiler package)
-----------------------------------------------------------------------

* ``ssa``  -- :func:`to_ssa`.  Legal on a lowered module and, as an
  idempotent canonicalization (clone + deterministic renumbering), on an
  already-SSA module.
* ``dce``  -- :func:`eliminate_dead_code`.  Its documented precondition is
  an SSA module: applying it before ``ssa`` raises ``ValueError``.
* instruction selection is the final :func:`render_module` and is fixed
  last.

The default optimization pipeline is ``ssa, dce, ssa``: the SSA-dependent
optimization (DCE) sits after SSA construction, and a trailing SSA
canonicalization compacts the numbering holes DCE may leave so the emitted
IR is the canonical fixed point of the sequence.  Alternative legal orders
differ only in the middle (extra normalization, an extra fixpoint DCE, or an
ssa/dce interleaving); the no-DCE order ``ssa`` is legal as well.

Observables
-----------

The language has no I/O statement, so the ordered trace of executed calls
``(callee, positional args)`` is the standard-output surrogate -- the only
side effect the language can have (it is also the observable used by
``test_semantic_equivalence.py``).  An outcome is one of:

* normal termination: return value (``None`` for ``void``) + call trace;
* a runtime fault: error category, trigger site, the operands at the fault,
  and the call trace produced *before* the fault.

The language's grammar already includes ``div``/``mod``; the single runtime
error the language defines is a zero divisor.  Division and modulo follow
truncation toward zero (the remainder satisfies ``a == (a/b)*b + a%b``).
There is no array or indexing construct, so no bounds error exists in this
language subset, and no undefined-behavior sample is used: every faulting
instruction's result is consumed (returned, branched on or accumulated), so
no legal order can legally delete it.

A fault site is identified independently of SSA numbering by
``(function name, block label, operator, ordinal of the BinOp among the
BinOps of its block)``: block labels are assigned by the lowering DFS and
preserved by ``to_ssa`` and DCE, and the relative order of surviving
BinOps is preserved as well.  Every faulting block in this suite contains a
single faulting BinOp, so the site is unambiguous.

All inputs are fixed literal argument tuples; the pipeline has no random
or environment-dependent behavior, hence there is no seed to pin.
"""
import copy
import unittest

from compiler_ir import (
    BinOp,
    Branch,
    Call,
    Const,
    Copy,
    Jump,
    Module,
    Return,
    Slot,
    Temp,
    TypeCheckError,
    UndefinedSymbolError,
    eliminate_dead_code,
    lower_module,
    render_module,
    to_ssa,
)

from test_pipeline import (
    arith,
    assign,
    bool_,
    call,
    compare,
    func,
    if_,
    int_,
    let,
    param,
    program,
    ret,
    var,
    while_,
)


# ==========================================================================
# IR interpreter with ordered call output and defined runtime faults
# ==========================================================================


_STEP_LIMIT = 100_000


class RuntimeFault(Exception):
    """A runtime error defined by the language.

    Carries the error ``category``, the numbering-independent ``site``
    ``(function, block label, operator, binop ordinal)``, the operand
    values at the fault, and the call trace observed before it fired.
    """

    def __init__(self, category, function, block_label, operator, ordinal,
                 left, right, output):
        self.category = category
        self.function = function
        self.block_label = block_label
        self.operator = operator
        self.ordinal = ordinal
        self.left = left
        self.right = right
        self.site = (function, block_label, operator, ordinal)
        self.output = list(output)
        super().__init__(
            f"{category} at {function}:{block_label} {operator} "
            f"({left!r}, {right!r})"
        )


ZERO_DIVISOR = "division-by-zero"


def _trunc_div(a: int, b: int):
    """Integer division truncated toward zero; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
    if b == 0:
        raise ZeroDivisionError
    quotient = abs(a) // abs(b)
    if (a < 0) != (b < 0):
        quotient = -quotient
    return quotient


def _trunc_mod(a: int, b: int):
    """Truncated-toward-zero remainder; raises ZeroDivisionError."""
    if b == 0:
        raise ZeroDivisionError
    return a - _trunc_div(a, b) * b


_ARITH = {
    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
    "div": _trunc_div,
    "mod": _trunc_mod,
}

_COMPARE = {
    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
}


def _assert(condition: bool, message: str) -> None:
    if not condition:
        raise AssertionError(message)


class _Interpreter:
    """Execute a lowered :class:`Module` of either SSA flavor.

    Mirrors the interpreter in ``test_semantic_equivalence.py`` but adds
    ``div``/``mod`` and converts their zero-divisor trap into a
    :class:`RuntimeFault` with a numbering-independent site.
    """

    def __init__(self, module: Module):
        _assert(isinstance(module, Module),
                f"interpreter expects a Module, got {type(module).__name__}")
        self.ssa = bool(module.ssa)
        self._functions = {fn_.name: fn_ for fn_ in module.functions}

    def run(self, entry: str, arguments):
        fn_ = self._functions.get(entry)
        _assert(fn_ is not None, f"unknown entry function {entry!r}")
        arguments = tuple(arguments)
        _assert(
            len(arguments) == len(fn_.params),
            f"entry {entry!r} expects {len(fn_.params)} argument(s), "
            f"got {len(arguments)}",
        )
        trace: list = []
        value = self._invoke(fn_, arguments, trace)
        return value, trace

    def _invoke(self, fn_, arguments, trace: list):
        definitions: dict = {}
        slots: dict = {}
        temps: dict = {}

        for parameter, argument in zip(fn_.params, arguments):
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(parameter.temp is not None,
                        f"SSA parameter {parameter.name!r} has no definition")
                definitions[id(parameter.temp)] = argument
            else:
                slots[parameter.slot.id] = argument

        def write_ref(ref, value) -> None:
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp) and not isinstance(
                    ref, Slot),
                    f"{fn_.name}: non-Temp definition {ref!r} in SSA IR")
                definitions[id(ref)] = value
            elif isinstance(ref, Slot):
                slots[ref.id] = value
            else:
                temps[id(ref)] = value

        def read(ref):
            if isinstance(ref, Slot):
                _assert(ref.id in slots,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined slot {ref}")
                return slots[ref.id]
            if self.ssa:
                _assert(isinstance(ref, Temp),
                        f"{fn_.name}: SSA read of non-Temp value {ref!r}")
                _assert(id(ref) in definitions,
                        f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined SSA value {ref}")
                return definitions[id(ref)]
            _assert(id(ref) in temps,
                    f"{fn_.name}: read of undefined temporary {ref}")
            return temps[id(ref)]

        def execute(instruction, block, binop_index) -> None:
            if isinstance(instruction, Const):
                write_ref(instruction.dest, instruction.value)
            elif isinstance(instruction, Copy):
                write_ref(instruction.dest, read(instruction.src))
            elif isinstance(instruction, BinOp):
                left = read(instruction.left)
                right = read(instruction.right)
                try:
                    value = _apply_binop(instruction, left, right, fn_.name)
                except ZeroDivisionError:
                    raise RuntimeFault(
                        ZERO_DIVISOR, fn_.name, block.label,
                        instruction.operator, binop_index[id(instruction)],
                        left, right, trace,
                    )
                write_ref(instruction.dest, value)
            elif isinstance(instruction, Call):
                callee = self._functions.get(instruction.name)
                _assert(callee is not None,
                        f"{fn_.name}: call to unknown function "
                        f"{instruction.name!r}")
                values = tuple(read(operand) for operand in instruction.args)
                _assert(
                    len(values) == len(callee.params),
                    f"call to {instruction.name!r}: run-time arity mismatch",
                )
                trace.append((instruction.name, values))
                write_ref(instruction.dest,
                          self._invoke(callee, values, trace))
            else:
                _assert(False,
                        f"{fn_.name}: unknown instruction {instruction!r}")

        known_blocks = {id(block) for block in fn_.blocks}
        block = fn_.entry
        previous = None
        steps_left = _STEP_LIMIT

        while True:
            _assert(steps_left > 0,
                    f"{fn_.name}: step budget exhausted "
                    "(program does not terminate?)")
            steps_left -= 1

            if self.ssa:
                pending = []
                for phi in block.phis:
                    _assert(previous is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi in entry block "
                            "has no predecessor edge")
                    source = phi.entries.get(previous)
                    _assert(source is not None,
                            f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi {phi.dest} has "
                            f"no incoming value from {previous.label}")
                    pending.append((phi.dest, read(source)))
                for destination, value in pending:
                    definitions[id(destination)] = value
            else:
                _assert(not block.phis,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: phi node in non-SSA IR")

            # Numbering-independent ordinal of each BinOp among the block's
            # BinOps (DCE preserves their relative order).  BinOp nodes are
            # mutable dataclasses and therefore unhashable, so key by id.
            binop_index = {
                id(ins): ordinal
                for ordinal, ins in enumerate(
                    ins for ins in block.instructions
                    if isinstance(ins, BinOp)
                )
            }
            for instruction in block.instructions:
                execute(instruction, block, binop_index)

            terminator = block.terminator
            _assert(terminator is not None,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: missing terminator")

            if isinstance(terminator, Return):
                return None if terminator.value is None else read(
                    terminator.value)

            if isinstance(terminator, Jump):
                _assert(id(terminator.target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: jump to unknown block "
                        f"{terminator.target.label}")
                previous, block = block, terminator.target
                continue

            if isinstance(terminator, Branch):
                condition = read(terminator.cond)
                _assert(isinstance(condition, bool),
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch on non-bool "
                        f"value {condition!r}")
                target = (terminator.true_target if condition
                          else terminator.false_target)
                _assert(id(target) in known_blocks,
                        f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: branch to unknown block "
                        f"{target.label}")
                previous, block = block, target
                continue

            _assert(False,
                    f"{fn_.name}:{block.label}: unknown terminator")


def _apply_binop(instruction: BinOp, left, right, fn_name: str):
    if instruction.kind == "arith":
        _assert(type(left) is int and type(right) is int,
                f"{fn_name}: arithmetic {instruction.operator!r} on "
                f"non-int operands {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _ARITH.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported arithmetic operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    if instruction.kind == "compare":
        _assert(type(left) == type(right),
                f"{fn_name}: comparison {instruction.operator!r} between "
                f"mismatched value types {left!r}, {right!r}")
        operation = _COMPARE.get(instruction.operator)
        _assert(operation is not None,
                f"{fn_name}: unsupported comparison operator "
                f"{instruction.operator!r}")
        return operation(left, right)

    _assert(False, f"{fn_name}: unknown BinOp kind {instruction.kind!r}")


class Outcome:
    """Observable result of one run: either a normal value or a fault."""

    def __init__(self, kind, value=None, output=(), category=None,
                 site=None, operands=None):
        self.kind = kind  # "normal" | "fault"
        self.value = value
        self.output = list(output)
        self.category = category
        self.site = site
        self.operands = operands

    @classmethod
    def normal(cls, value, output):
        return cls("normal", value=value, output=output)

    @classmethod
    def fault(cls, error: RuntimeFault):
        return cls(
            "fault", output=error.output, category=error.category,
            site=error.site, operands=(error.left, error.right),
        )

    def __eq__(self, other):
        if not isinstance(other, Outcome):
            return NotImplemented
        return (
            self.kind, self.value, self.output,
            self.category, self.site, self.operands,
        ) == (
            other.kind, other.value, other.output,
            other.category, other.site, other.operands,
        )

    def __repr__(self):
        if self.kind == "normal":
            return f"Outcome.normal(value={self.value!r}, output={self.output!r})"
        return (
            f"Outcome.fault(category={self.category!r}, site={self.site!r}, "
            f"operands={self.operands!r}, output={self.output!r})"
        )


def _interpret(module: Module, entry: str, arguments) -> Outcome:
    try:
        value, trace = _Interpreter(module).run(entry, arguments)
    except RuntimeFault as fault:
        return Outcome.fault(fault)
    return Outcome.normal(value, trace)


# ==========================================================================
# Pass schedules (existing passes only; stage contracts enforced)
# ==========================================================================


# SSA construction, DCE, then a final SSA canonicalization (clone +
# deterministic renumbering), which makes the emitted IR the fixed point of
# the whole sequence: DCE may leave numbering holes, and the trailing ssa
# pass compacts them without changing structure or semantics.
DEFAULT_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa")

# Legal alternatives: extra early normalization, an explicit DCE fixpoint
# repeat, and an ssa/dce interleaving -- all end in the canonicalizing ssa
# pass, so each is a fixed point of its own sequence.
ALT_DOUBLE_SSA = ("ssa", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT = ("ssa", "dce", "dce", "ssa")
ALT_INTERLEAVE = ("ssa", "dce", "ssa", "dce", "ssa")
# Legal but less optimizing: construction + canonicalization only.
NO_DCE_ORDER = ("ssa",)
# The README-documented core without the trailing canonicalization: legal,
# used for cross-order semantics and determinism (its endpoint may carry
# numbering holes and is compared on observables, not text).
RAW_CORE_ORDER = ("ssa", "dce")

LEGAL_ORDERS = {
    "default ssa,dce,ssa": DEFAULT_ORDER,
    "alt ssa,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_DOUBLE_SSA,
    "alt ssa,dce,dce,ssa": ALT_DCE_FIXPOINT,
    "alt ssa,dce,ssa,dce,ssa": ALT_INTERLEAVE,
    "no-dce ssa": NO_DCE_ORDER,
    "raw core ssa,dce": RAW_CORE_ORDER,
}

# Orders whose endpoint is the canonical fixed point used by the strict
# idempotence test.
IDEMPOTENT_ORDERS = {
    name: order for name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items()
    if name != "raw core ssa,dce"
}


def apply_order(module: Module, order) -> Module:
    """Apply ``order`` (a tuple of pass names) to ``module``.

    :raises ValueError: if a pass name is unknown, if instruction selection
        appears anywhere but the end, or if ``dce`` is scheduled before the
        first ``ssa`` (DCE requires an SSA module).
    """
    ssa_seen = bool(getattr(module, "ssa", False))
    for index, name in enumerate(order):
        if name == "ssa":
            module = to_ssa(module)
            ssa_seen = True
        elif name == "dce":
            if not ssa_seen:
                raise ValueError(
                    "pass order violates precondition: 'dce' requires an SSA "
                    "module, but no 'ssa' pass precedes it"
                )
            module = eliminate_dead_code(module)
        elif name == "isel":
            raise ValueError(
                "pass order violates stage contract: instruction selection "
                "('isel') must be the final stage"
            )
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"unknown pass in order: {name!r}")
    return module


def compile_ast(ast: dict, order):
    """Compile a fresh copy of ``ast`` through lowering and ``order``.

    Returns ``(unoptimized_module, optimized_module, target_text)`` where
    the target text is instruction selection (rendering) run last.
    """
    lowered = lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast))
    optimized = apply_order(lowered, order)
    return lowered, optimized, render_module(optimized)


def structural_signature(module: Module):
    """Numbering-independent structural fingerprint of a module."""
    signature = []
    for fn_ in module.functions:
        blocks = []
        for block in fn_.blocks:
            instructions = []
            for ins in block.instructions:
                if isinstance(ins, Const):
                    instructions.append(("const", ins.value))
                elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
                    instructions.append(("copy",))
                elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
                    instructions.append((ins.kind, ins.operator))
                elif isinstance(ins, Call):
                    instructions.append(("call", ins.name, len(ins.args)))
            terminator = type(block.terminator).__name__
            blocks.append((
                block.id, terminator, len(block.phis),
                tuple(instructions),
            ))
        signature.append((
            fn_.name, fn_.ret_type,
            tuple((p.name, p.temp.type if p.temp is not None
                   else p.slot.type) for p in fn_.params),
            tuple(blocks),
        ))
    return tuple(signature)

def _emit_function(name="emit"):
    return func(name, [param("v", "int")], "int", [ret(var("v"))])


# A) Constants and phi propagation at a branch convergence.
#
# `a` is the same dominating constant on BOTH outgoing edges, so its merge
# phi is trivial (one incoming SSA value) and is pruned during SSA
# construction; the returned value is that constant propagated through the
# join.  `b` carries genuinely different values per edge and needs a real
# merge phi consumed by a side-effecting call.
def _join_program():
    return program(
        func("join", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
            let("k", "int", int_(7)),
            let("a", "int", int_(0)),
            if_(var("c"), [assign("a", var("k"))],
                 [assign("a", var("k"))]),
            let("b", "int", int_(0)),
            if_(var("c"),
                [assign("b", arith("add", var("x"), int_(1)))],
                [assign("b", arith("sub", var("x"), int_(1)))]),
            let("s", "int", call("emit", [var("b")])),
            ret(arith("add", var("a"), var("s"))),
        ]),
        _emit_function(),
    )


# B) Deletable pure computations vs. still-side-effecting expressions.
#
# `d` and `junk` are pure chains nobody consumes: DCE deletes them (and
# their constants), but BOTH calls remain roots even though `ignored`'s
# result is never read -- deleting either would drop observable output.
def _clean_program():
    return program(
        func("clean", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
            let("d", "int",
                arith("mul", arith("add", int_(1), int_(2)), int_(3))),
            let("keptarg", "int", arith("add", var("n"), int_(10))),
            let("v", "int", call("observe", [var("keptarg")])),
            let("ignored", "int", call("observe", [int_(99)])),
            let("junk", "int",
                arith("add", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(3)), var("d"))),
            ret(arith("add", var("v"), int_(4))),
        ]),
        _emit_function("observe"),
    )


# C) Loop-invariant value plus a conditional branch inside the loop.
#
# `base` is loop invariant and defined before the header; the loop still
# carries real header phis for `i` and `total`, and the in-loop if makes the
# side-effecting call happen only on iterations that take its else edge.
def _loop_program():
    return program(
        func("loopsum", [param("n", "int"), param("k", "int")], "int", [
            let("base", "int", arith("add", var("k"), int_(1))),
            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
                if_(compare("gt", var("i"), int_(1)),
                    [assign("total", arith(
                        "add",
                        arith("add", var("total"), var("base")),
                        var("i")))],
                    [
                        let("t", "int", call("ping", [var("i")])),
                        assign("total", arith("add", var("total"), var("t"))),
                    ]),
                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
            ]),
            ret(var("total")),
        ]),
        _emit_function("ping"),
    )


# D) An inlineable call with dead code introduced after it.
#
# `dbl` is a trivial inline candidate; no pass order actually inlines it, so
# every order keeps the call and its observable position.  The pure
# computations built AFTER the call (`junk1`, `junk2`) are dead and vanish
# under DCE, while the later side-effecting call `after` is preserved.
def _around_program():
    return program(
        func("around", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
            let("v", "int", call("dbl", [arith("add", var("n"), int_(1))])),
            let("junk1", "int", arith("mul", var("v"), int_(9))),
            let("junk2", "int", arith("add", var("junk1"), int_(5))),
            let("w", "int", call("after", [var("v")])),
            ret(var("v")),
        ]),
        func("dbl", [param("x", "int")], "int",
             [ret(arith("mul", var("x"), int_(2)))]),
        _emit_function("after"),
    )


# E1) Zero divisor on one arm of a branch; the other arm terminates fine.
def _guarded_fault_program():
    return program(
        func("guarded", [param("c", "bool"), param("x", "int")], "int", [
            let("d", "int", int_(0)),
            if_(var("c"),
                [
                    let("e", "int", call("emit", [int_(1)])),
                    let("q", "int", arith("div", var("x"), var("d"))),
                    ret(arith("add", var("q"), var("e"))),
                ],
                [
                    let("e2", "int", call("emit", [int_(2)])),
                    ret(var("e2")),
                ]),
        ]),
        _emit_function(),
    )


# E2) Zero divisor reached inside a loop after observable output.
def _loop_fault_program():
    return program(
        func("looptrap", [param("n", "int")], "int", [
            let("total", "int", int_(0)),
            let("i", "int", int_(0)),
            while_(compare("lt", var("i"), var("n")), [
                let("e", "int", call("emit", [var("i")])),
                let("q", "int",
                    arith("div", int_(100),
                          arith("sub", int_(2), var("i")))),
                assign("total", arith("add", var("total"), var("q"))),
                assign("i", arith("add", var("i"), int_(1))),
            ]),
            ret(var("total")),
        ]),
        _emit_function(),
    )


# E3) Modulo by zero after a side effect; single-block fault site.
def _mod_fault_program():
    return program(
        func("modfall", [param("x", "int")], "int", [
            let("z", "int", int_(0)),
            let("e", "int", call("emit", [var("x")])),
            let("r", "int", arith("mod", var("x"), var("z"))),
            ret(arith("add", var("r"), var("e"))),
        ]),
        _emit_function(),
    )


# (label, AST builder, entry, argument tuple, pinned expected Outcome) -- the
# pin anchors ground truth independently of the non-SSA/SSA cross-check.
_CASES = [
    (
        "branch-join constants and phi propagation",
        _join_program, "join", (True, 10),
        Outcome.normal(18, [("emit", (11,))]),
    ),
    (
        "branch-join constants and phi propagation (other edge)",
        _join_program, "join", (False, 10),
        Outcome.normal(16, [("emit", (9,))]),
    ),
    (
        "deletable computations vs side effects",
        _clean_program, "clean", (5,),
        Outcome.normal(19, [("observe", (15,)), ("observe", (99,))]),
    ),
    (
        "deletable computations vs side effects (negative arg)",
        _clean_program, "clean", (-3,),
        Outcome.normal(11, [("observe", (7,)), ("observe", (99,))]),
    ),
    (
        "loop invariant with inner branch",
        _loop_program, "loopsum", (4, 100),
        Outcome.normal(
            208, [("ping", (0,)), ("ping", (1,))]),
    ),
    (
        "loop zero trips",
        _loop_program, "loopsum", (0, 100),
        Outcome.normal(0, []),
    ),
    (
        "inlineable call followed by dead code",
        _around_program, "around", (4,),
        Outcome.normal(10, [("dbl", (5,)), ("after", (10,))]),
    ),
    (
        "branch-arm division by zero",
        _guarded_fault_program, "guarded", (True, 7),
        Outcome(
            "fault",
            output=[("emit", (1,))],
            category=ZERO_DIVISOR,
            site=("guarded", "b1", "div", 0),
            operands=(7, 0),
        ),
    ),
    (
        "branch other arm terminates normally",
        _guarded_fault_program, "guarded", (False, 7),
        Outcome.normal(2, [("emit", (2,))]),
    ),
    (
        "loop division by zero after output",
        _loop_fault_program, "looptrap", (5,),
        Outcome(
            "fault",
            output=[("emit", (0,)), ("emit", (1,)), ("emit", (2,))],
            category=ZERO_DIVISOR,
            # b2 computes the divisor (2 - i) first (BinOp ordinal 0) and
            # then the division (ordinal 1) that actually faults.
            site=("looptrap", "b2", "div", 1),
            operands=(100, 0),
        ),
    ),
    (
        "loop exits just before the faulting iteration",
        _loop_fault_program, "looptrap", (2,),
        Outcome.normal(150, [("emit", (0,)), ("emit", (1,))]),
    ),
    (
        "modulo by zero",
        _mod_fault_program, "modfall", (5,),
        Outcome(
            "fault",
            output=[("emit", (5,))],

            operands=(5, 0),

]


# ==========================================================================
# Failure formatting: sample, order, and first differing observable
# ==========================================================================


def _first_difference(expected: Outcome, actual: Outcome):
    """Name the first observable that differs, in comparison order."""
    if expected.kind != actual.kind:
        return "termination kind", expected.kind, actual.kind
    if expected.output != actual.output:
        return "standard output (ordered call trace)", expected.output, \
            actual.output
    if expected.kind == "fault":
        if expected.category != actual.category:
            return "runtime error category", expected.category, \
                actual.category
        if expected.site != actual.site:
            return "runtime error trigger site", expected.site, actual.site
        if expected.operands != actual.operands:
            return "runtime error operands", expected.operands, \
                actual.operands
    else:
        if expected.value != actual.value:
            return "return value", expected.value, actual.value
    return None


def _mismatch_message(label, order_name, entry, arguments, expected, actual):
    diff = _first_difference(expected, actual)
    header = (
        f"semantic mismatch for sample {label!r}, order {order_name!r}, "
        f"entry {entry!r}, arguments {arguments!r}"
    )
    if diff is None:
        return header
    field, wanted, got = diff
    return (
        f"{header}\n"
        f"first differing observable: {field}\n"
        f"  expected: {wanted!r}\n"
        f"  actual:   {got!r}\n"
        f"baseline outcome: {expected!r}\n"
        f"this order:       {actual!r}"
    )

class CrossOrderSemanticsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_every_legal_order_matches_unoptimized_baseline(self):
        for label, builder, entry, arguments, pinned in _CASES:
            ast = builder()
            with self.subTest(sample=label):
                baseline = _interpret(
                    lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast)), entry, arguments)

                # The pin is independent ground truth; baseline must meet it.
                diff = _first_difference(pinned, baseline)
                self.assertIsNone(
                    diff,
                    msg=(f"sample {label!r}: unoptimized baseline disagrees "
                         f"with pinned expectation: {diff}\n"
                         f"baseline: {baseline!r}\n"
                         f"pinned:   {pinned!r}"),
                )

                for order_name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items():
                    with self.subTest(order=order_name):
                        _l, optimized, _t = compile_ast(ast, order)
                        outcome = _interpret(optimized, entry, arguments)
                        diff = _first_difference(baseline, outcome)
                        self.assertIsNone(
                            diff,
                            msg=_mismatch_message(
                                label, order_name, entry, arguments,
                                baseline, outcome),
                        )

    def test_target_text_is_never_the_cross_order_correctness_basis(self):
        # The dead-computation sample lays out differently with and without
        # DCE: that text difference is allowed.  Semantics still agree.
        ast = _clean_program()
        _l, optimized, opt_text = compile_ast(ast, DEFAULT_ORDER)
        _l2, unoptimized_ssa, no_dce_text = compile_ast(ast, NO_DCE_ORDER)

        # The pure `(1+2)*3` chain is present without DCE but gone with it.
        # Match a standalone literal 1 ("const 10" must not count).
        const_one = r"const 1(?!\d)"
        self.assertRegex(no_dce_text, const_one)
        self.assertNotRegex(opt_text, const_one)
        self.assertNotEqual(no_dce_text, opt_text)

        for arguments in ((5,), (-3,)):
            a = _interpret(unoptimized_ssa, "clean", arguments)
            b = _interpret(optimized, "clean", arguments)
            self.assertEqual(
                a, b,
                msg="text layouts differ by design; outcomes must not",
            )

    def test_fault_category_site_and_prefix_agree_across_orders(self):
        fault_cases = [
            case for case in _CASES if case[4].kind == "fault"
        ]
        self.assertTrue(fault_cases, "suite must include runtime-fault cases")
        for label, builder, entry, arguments, pinned in fault_cases:
            ast = builder()
            baseline = _interpret(
                lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast)), entry, arguments)
            self.assertEqual(baseline.kind, "fault")
            self.assertEqual(baseline.category, pinned.category)
            self.assertEqual(baseline.site, pinned.site)
            for order_name, order in LEGAL_ORDERS.items():
                _l, optimized, _t = compile_ast(ast, order)
                outcome = _interpret(optimized, entry, arguments)
                diff = _first_difference(baseline, outcome)
                self.assertIsNone(
                    diff,
                    msg=_mismatch_message(
                        label, order_name, entry, arguments,
                        baseline, outcome),
                )


class DeterminismTests(unittest.TestCase):

class IdempotenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_reapplying_same_sequence_is_a_noop(self):
        for label, builder, _entry, _args, _pin in _CASES:
            ast = builder()
            for order_name, order in IDEMPOTENT_ORDERS.items():
                with self.subTest(sample=label, order=order_name):
                    _l, once, text_once = compile_ast(ast, order)
                    self.assertTrue(once.ssa)

                    # Apply the very same sequence to the optimized result.
                    twice = apply_order(once, order)
                    text_twice = render_module(twice)
                    self.assertEqual(
                        text_once, text_twice,
                        msg=(f"{label!r} / {order_name!r}: canonical target "
                             "code changed on second application"),
                    )
                    self.assertEqual(
                        structural_signature(once),
                        structural_signature(twice),
                        msg=(f"{label!r} / {order_name!r}: canonical IR "
                             "structure changed on second application"),
                    )
                    self.assertIsNot(twice, once)

                    # A third application must be stable as well.
                    thrice = apply_order(twice, order)
                    self.assertEqual(
                        text_twice, render_module(thrice),
                        msg=f"{label!r} / {order_name!r}: not a fixed point",
                    )

    def test_individual_repeatable_passes_are_fixpoints(self):
        for label, builder, _entry, _args, _pin in _CASES:
            ast = builder()
            lowered = lower_module(copy.deepcopy(ast))
            ssa_once = to_ssa(lowered)
            ssa_twice = to_ssa(ssa_once)
            with self.subTest(sample=label, pass_="ssa"):
                self.assertEqual(
                    render_module(ssa_once), render_module(ssa_twice))
                self.assertEqual(
                    structural_signature(ssa_once),
                    structural_signature(ssa_twice),
                )

            dce_once = eliminate_dead_code(ssa_once)
            dce_twice = eliminate_dead_code(dce_once)
            with self.subTest(sample=label, pass_="dce"):
                self.assertEqual(
                    render_module(dce_once), render_module(dce_twice))
                self.assertEqual(
                    structural_signature(dce_once),
                    structural_signature(dce_twice),
                )

    def test_raw_core_reaches_canonical_fixed_point(self):
        # ssa,dce may leave numbering holes; the trailing canonicalizing ssa
        # pass is precisely what turns it into the default pipeline's stable
        # endpoint, and iterating ssa,dce from there changes nothing.
        for label, builder, _entry, _args, _pin in _CASES:
            ast = builder()
            lowered, core, _text = compile_ast(ast, RAW_CORE_ORDER)
            # DCE alone is already a structural fixpoint even with holes.
            self.assertEqual(
                render_module(core),
                render_module(eliminate_dead_code(core)),
            )
            canonical = to_ssa(core)
            cycled = to_ssa(eliminate_dead_code(canonical))
            self.assertEqual(
                render_module(canonical), render_module(cycled),
                msg=(f"{label!r}: default-style endpoint is not the "
                     "canonical fixed point"),
            )

    def test_inputs_are_not_mutated_by_reapplication(self):
        for label, builder, _entry, _args, _pin in _CASES:
            ast = builder()
            lowered, once, text_before = compile_ast(ast, DEFAULT_ORDER)
            lowered_text_before = render_module(lowered)
            apply_order(once, DEFAULT_ORDER)
            self.assertEqual(render_module(once), text_before)
            self.assertEqual(render_module(lowered), lowered_text_before)

            self.assertTrue(text.endswith("\n"))
            self.assertIn("function clean", text)


class DceShapeOnFocusedFormsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    """Structural pins for the forms where passes genuinely interact."""

    def _caller(self, module: Module, name: str):
        return next(fn_ for fn_ in module.functions if fn_.name == name)

                 if isinstance(ins, Call)]

                  for ins in b.instructions if isinstance(ins, Const)}
        self.assertEqual(consts, {10, 99, 4})

        binops = [
            (ins.kind, ins.operator) for b in caller.blocks
            for ins in b.instructions if isinstance(ins, BinOp)
        ]
        self.assertEqual(binops, [("arith", "add"), ("arith", "add")])

        _l, optimized, _t = compile_ast(_around_program(), DEFAULT_ORDER)

1	"""SSA constant folding and propagation.
2	
3	The entry point :func:`fold_constants` takes an SSA :class:`Module`
4	produced by :func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa` and returns a brand new SSA
5	:class:`Module` in which known literal values are propagated along the SSA
6	def-use chains; the input module is never mutated and shares no mutable
7	function, block, instruction or phi container with the result.
8	
9	A value is *known* when it is statically provably a fixed literal:
10	
11	* a ``Const`` definition is known directly;
12	* an arithmetic or compare ``BinOp`` folds only when both operands are
13	  known, and its result becomes known for subsequent definitions;
14	* a ``Phi`` folds exactly when the literals arriving on *every* reachable
15	  predecessor edge are all known and identical (a phi's own result is not
16	  an incoming definition and cannot occur there).
17	
18	Arithmetic covers ``add``, ``sub``, ``mul``, ``div`` and ``mod``, and
19	comparisons ``eq``, ``ne``, ``lt``, ``le``, ``gt`` and ``ge``; the int and
20	bool result types are preserved.  Integer division truncates toward zero
21	and the remainder satisfies ``a == div(a,b) * b + mod(a,b)``.  A known
22	zero divisor must not be folded away: the original ``BinOp`` is kept so the
23	runtime trap and its position in the instruction stream are neither
24	advanced, swallowed nor rewritten.  A ``Call`` result is always unknown,
25	and the call instruction together with its relative order is untouched.
26	
27	Because a loop header phi can look constant on its (constant) entry edge
28	before the back edge is analyzed, literals are tracked in a monotone
29	three-level lattice -- unknown, constant ``k``, and non-constant -- solved
30	to a fixpoint: a phi starts unknown, sinks to its first seen literal and
31	reaches non-constant as soon as two edges disagree (or an edge carries a
32	non-constant value).  This is the lattice half of sparse conditional
33	constant propagation; the reachability half is deliberately absent, so no
34	blocks are deleted, no constant ``Branch`` becomes a ``Jump``, and
35	definitions made pointless by folding are left in place for
36	:func:`~compiler_ir.dce.eliminate_dead_code` to remove.
37	
38	Folded definitions become a ``Const`` in their *own* SSA slot (the same
39	value number), so no operand needs rewriting: every existing use already
40	names that slot, which now holds the literal.  A folded phi loses its phi
41	node and contributes its ``Const`` ahead of the block's ordinary
42	instructions (in phi order), matching where the merge value is defined.
43	
44	Function order, signatures, parameters, block labels and order,
45	terminators, phi order, the relative order of all instructions and the
46	existing SSA numbers are all preserved; the output therefore has the same
47	definition slots as the input.  Applying the pass again gives a
48	structurally and textually identical fixed point.
49	
50	A non-:class:`Module` object raises :class:`TypeError`; a non-SSA
51	:class:`Module` raises :class:`ValueError`.

53	from .ir_nodes import (
54	    BinOp,
55	    Block,
56	    Branch,
57	    Call,
58	    Const,
59	    Copy,
60	    Function,
61	    Jump,
62	    Module,
63	    Parameter,

70	# Per-value lattice levels (keyed by SSA value id):
71	#   absent/None      -> unknown (not yet constrained; a phi's initial state)
72	#   int/bool literal -> known to be exactly that literal
73	#   _BOTTOM          -> not a compile-time constant
74	_BOTTOM = object()
75	
76	
77	def _same_literal(a, b) -> bool:
78	    # Type-strict equality: the SSA type system never lets an int and a
79	    # bool meet, but Python's ``True == 1`` must not merge them if a
80	    # malformed module ever does.
81	    return type(a) is type(b) and a == b
82	
83	
84	def fold_constants(module: Module) -> Module:
85	    """Return a new SSA :class:`Module` with literals folded and propagated.
86	
87	    The input module is left untouched; the result shares no mutable
88	    function, block, instruction or phi object with it.  The empty module
89	    and modules without foldable definitions come back as independent,
90	    content-equivalent copies.
91	
92	    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module` instance.
93	    :raises ValueError: if ``module`` is not in SSA form.
94	    """
95	    if not isinstance(module, Module):
96	        raise TypeError(
97	            "fold_constants expects a Module, got "
98	            f"{type(module).__name__}"
99	        )
100	    if not getattr(module, "ssa", False):
101	        raise ValueError("fold_constants expects an SSA Module")
102	    return Module(
103	        [_Folder(func).build() for func in module.functions], ssa=True
104	    )
105	
106	
107	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
108	# Arithmetic / comparison semantics (truncated toward zero, like the runtime)
109	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
110	
111	
112	def _trunc_div(a: int, b: int) -> int:
113	    """Integer division truncated toward zero.
114	
115	    Only called for a provably non-zero divisor; a zero divisor is handled
116	    by the caller so the faulting instruction stays in the stream.
117	    """
118	    quotient = abs(a) // abs(b)
119	    if (a < 0) != (b < 0):
120	        quotient = -quotient
121	    return quotient
122	
123	
124	def _trunc_mod(a: int, b: int) -> int:
125	    # a == div(a,b) * b + mod(a,b)
126	    return a - _trunc_div(a, b) * b
127	
128	
129	_ARITH = {
130	    "add": lambda a, b: a + b,
131	    "sub": lambda a, b: a - b,
132	    "mul": lambda a, b: a * b,
133	    "div": _trunc_div,
134	    "mod": _trunc_mod,
135	}
136	
137	_COMPARE = {
138	    "eq": lambda a, b: a == b,
139	    "ne": lambda a, b: a != b,
140	    "lt": lambda a, b: a < b,
141	    "le": lambda a, b: a <= b,
142	    "gt": lambda a, b: a > b,
143	    "ge": lambda a, b: a >= b,
144	}

146	
147	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
148	# Per-function fixpoint and output construction
149	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
150	
151	
152	class _Folder:
153	    def __init__(self, func: Function):
154	        self.func = func
155	        self.lattice: dict = {}
156	        # Definition id -> user nodes that re-read it, tagged by kind.
157	        self.users: dict = {}
158	        self.worklist: list = []
159	
160	    # -- lattice ------------------------------------------------------------
161	
162	    def get(self, value):
163	        return self.lattice.get(id(value))
164	
165	    def constrain(self, value, level) -> bool:
166	        """Monotonically move ``value`` toward ``level``.
167	
168	        Returns whether its level changed.  ``None`` (unknown) never
169	        constrains anything; two disagreeing literals collapse to
170	        ``_BOTTOM``.
171	        """
172	        if level is None:
173	            return False
174	        current = self.lattice.get(id(value))
175	        if current is _BOTTOM:
176	            return False
177	        if current is None:
178	            self.lattice[id(value)] = level
179	            return True
180	        if level is not _BOTTOM and _same_literal(current, level):
181	            return False
182	        self.lattice[id(value)] = _BOTTOM
183	        return True
184	
185	    def note_user(self, operand, user) -> None:
186	        self.users.setdefault(id(operand), []).append(user)
187	
188	    def enqueue_users(self, value) -> None:
189	        self.worklist.extend(self.users.get(id(value), ()))
190	
191	    # -- transfer functions -------------------------------------------------
192	
193	    def phi_level(self, phi: Phi):
194	        """Join over every reachable incoming edge."""
195	        result = None
196	        for value in phi.entries.values():
197	            level = self.get(value)
198	            if level is _BOTTOM:
199	                return _BOTTOM
200	            if level is None:
201	                continue
202	            if result is None:
203	                result = level
204	            elif not _same_literal(result, level):
205	                return _BOTTOM
206	        return result
207	
208	    def binop_level(self, ins: BinOp):
209	        left = self.get(ins.left)
210	        right = self.get(ins.right)
211	        if left is None or right is None:
212	            return None
213	        if left is _BOTTOM or right is _BOTTOM:
214	            return _BOTTOM

219	                # non-constant rather than folding the fault away.
220	                return _BOTTOM
221	            return _ARITH[ins.operator](left, right)
222	        return _COMPARE[ins.operator](left, right)
223	
224	    # -- fixpoint ------------------------------------------------------------
225	
226	    def solve(self) -> None:
227	        # Parameters are never statically known.
228	        for param in self.func.params:
229	            self.constrain(param.temp, _BOTTOM)
230	
231	        # Register users and seed every definition.  Traversal order is the
232	        # deterministic numbering order (blocks in id order, phis before
233	        # instructions); it affects only iteration count, not the fixpoint.
234	        for block in self.func.blocks:
235	            for phi in block.phis:
236	                for value in phi.entries.values():
237	                    self.note_user(value, ("phi", phi))
238	                self.worklist.append(("phi", phi))
239	            for ins in block.instructions:
240	                if isinstance(ins, Const):
241	                    self.worklist.append(("const", ins))
242	                elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
243	                    self.note_user(ins.left, ("binop", ins))
244	                    self.note_user(ins.right, ("binop", ins))
245	                    self.worklist.append(("binop", ins))
246	                elif isinstance(ins, Call):
247	                    # Call results are always unknown.
248	                    self.constrain(ins.dest, _BOTTOM)
249	                elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
250	                    self.note_user(ins.src, ("copy", ins))
251	                    self.worklist.append(("copy", ins))
252	
253	        while self.worklist:
254	            kind, node = self.worklist.pop()
255	            if kind == "const":
256	                changed = self.constrain(node.dest, node.value)
257	            elif kind == "binop":
258	                changed = self.constrain(node.dest, self.binop_level(node))
259	            elif kind == "copy":
260	                changed = self.constrain(node.dest, self.get(node.src))
261	            else:
262	                changed = self.constrain(node.dest, self.phi_level(node))
263	            if changed:
264	                self.enqueue_users(node.dest)
265	
266	    def is_constant(self, value):
267	        """The settled literal for ``value``, or None if not a constant."""
268	        level = self.lattice.get(id(value))
269	        if level is None or level is _BOTTOM:
270	            return None
271	        return level
272	
273	    # -- output --------------------------------------------------------------
274	
275	    def build(self) -> Function:
276	        self.solve()
277	
278	        new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in self.func.blocks]
279	        block_map = dict(zip(self.func.blocks, new_blocks))
280	
281	        # One fresh Temp per original definition, preserving original ids;
282	        # every existing operand keeps pointing at the same slot.
283	        value_map: dict = {}
284	
285	        def fresh(value: Temp) -> Temp:
286	            mapped = value_map.get(id(value))
287	            if mapped is None:
288	                mapped = Temp(value.id, value.type)
289	                value_map[id(value)] = mapped
290	            return mapped
291	
292	        for param in self.func.params:
293	            fresh(param.temp)
294	        for block in self.func.blocks:
295	            for phi in block.phis:
296	                fresh(phi.dest)
297	            for ins in block.instructions:
298	                fresh(ins.dest)
299	
300	        def map_value(value):
301	            if value is None:
302	                return None
303	            return value_map[id(value)]
304	
305	        for block, new_block in zip(self.func.blocks, new_blocks):
306	            # Folded phis become leading Consts (in phi order); surviving
307	            # phis keep their entries and predecessor order.
308	            for phi in block.phis:
309	                literal = self.is_constant(phi.dest)
310	                if literal is not None:
311	                    new_block.instructions.append(
312	                        Const(map_value(phi.dest), literal)
313	                    )
314	                else:
315	                    entries = {
316	                        block_map[pred]: map_value(value)
317	                        for pred, value in sorted(
318	                            phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
319	                        )
320	                    }
321	                    new_block.phis.append(
322	                        Phi(map_value(phi.dest), entries)
323	                    )
324	
325	            for ins in block.instructions:
326	                new_block.instructions.append(
327	                    self._clone_instruction(ins, map_value)
328	                )
329	
330	            term = block.terminator
331	            if isinstance(term, Return):
332	                new_block.terminator = Return(map_value(term.value))
333	            elif isinstance(term, Jump):
334	                new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
335	            elif isinstance(term, Branch):
336	                new_block.terminator = Branch(
337	                    map_value(term.cond),
338	                    block_map[term.true_target],
339	                    block_map[term.false_target],
340	                )
341	
342	        new_params = [
343	            Parameter(param.name, param.slot, map_value(param.temp))
344	            for param in self.func.params
345	        ]
346	
347	        return Function(
348	            self.func.name,
349	            new_params,
350	            self.func.ret_type,
351	            list(self.func.locals),
352	            new_blocks,
353	            block_map[self.func.entry],
354	            ssa=True,
355	        )

357	    def _clone_instruction(self, ins, map_value):
358	        if isinstance(ins, Const):
359	            return Const(map_value(ins.dest), ins.value)
360	        if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
361	            literal = self.is_constant(ins.dest)
362	            if literal is not None:
363	                return Const(map_value(ins.dest), literal)

365	                map_value(ins.dest), ins.operator,
366	                map_value(ins.left), map_value(ins.right),
367	                ins.kind, ins.type,
368	            )
369	        if isinstance(ins, Call):

371	                map_value(ins.dest), ins.name,

373	            )
374	        # Copy cannot survive to_ssa; handled defensively as pure aliasing.
375	        if isinstance(ins, Copy):

1	"""Dead-code elimination on pruned SSA form.
2	
3	The entry point :func:`eliminate_dead_code` takes an SSA :class:`Module`
4	produced by :func:`~compiler_ir.ssa.to_ssa` and returns a brand new SSA
5	:class:`Module` with unreachable definitions removed; the input module is
6	never mutated and shares no mutable function, block, instruction or phi
7	container with the result.
8	
9	Liveness is traced per function, definition-to-use, from fixed roots:
10	
11	* every operand of a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` terminator;
12	* every ``Call`` instruction, regardless of whether its result is used --
13	  the call itself and its position in the instruction stream are observable
14	  behavior -- together with all of its argument definitions.
15	
16	A ``Const``, ``BinOp`` or ``Phi`` that cannot reach one of those roots is
17	deleted.  The trace runs on the whole function at once, so chains feeding
18	only other dead definitions and closed phi cycles die together in one pass;
19	elimination is then repeated until no new dead definition appears.
20	
21	The pass is purely subtractive.  No constants are folded, branches
22	rewritten, blocks deleted or control flow reordered.  Function order,
23	signatures, parameters, return types, block labels and order, terminators,
24	the relative order of surviving instructions and the predecessor order of
25	surviving phis are all preserved, and SSA numbers of surviving values are
26	left untouched (the output may therefore contain numbering holes).
27	
28	Applying the pass to an already minimal module returns an independent,
29	structurally and textually equivalent copy, so a second
30	:func:`eliminate_dead_code` changes nothing.  A non-:class:`Module` object
31	raises :class:`TypeError`; a non-SSA :class:`Module` raises
32	:class:`ValueError`.
33	"""
34	from .ir_nodes import (
35	    BinOp,
36	    Block,
37	    Branch,
38	    Call,
39	    Const,
40	    Copy,
41	    Function,
42	    Jump,
43	    Module,
44	    Parameter,
45	    Phi,
46	    Return,
47	    Temp,
48	)
49	
50	
51	def eliminate_dead_code(module: Module) -> Module:
52	    """Return a new SSA :class:`Module` with dead definitions removed.
53	
54	    The input module is left untouched; the result shares no mutable
55	    function, block, instruction or phi object with it.
56	
57	    :raises TypeError: if ``module`` is not a :class:`Module` instance.
58	    :raises ValueError: if ``module`` is not in SSA form.
59	    """
60	    if not isinstance(module, Module):
61	        raise TypeError(
62	            "eliminate_dead_code expects a Module, got "
63	            f"{type(module).__name__}"
64	        )
65	    if not getattr(module, "ssa", False):
66	        raise ValueError("eliminate_dead_code expects an SSA Module")
67	    return Module(
68	        [_eliminate_in_function(func) for func in module.functions], ssa=True
69	    )
70	
71	
72	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
73	# Operand helpers (mirror the ones used by the SSA conversion)
74	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
75	
76	
77	def _operands(ins):
78	    if isinstance(ins, BinOp):
79	        return [ins.left, ins.right]
80	    if isinstance(ins, Call):
81	        return list(ins.args)
82	    # Const has no operands; a Copy cannot survive the non-SSA -> SSA
83	    # conversion (it folds into renaming) but is treated as pure anyway.
84	    if isinstance(ins, Copy):
85	        return [ins.src]
86	    return []
87	
88	
89	def _term_operands(term):
90	    if isinstance(term, Return) and term.value is not None:
91	        return [term.value]
92	    if isinstance(term, Branch):
93	        return [term.cond]
94	    return []
95	
96	
97	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
98	# Per-function elimination
99	# --------------------------------------------------------------------------
100	
101	
102	def _live_definitions(func: Function) -> set:
103	    """Return the ids of values live from the terminator/call roots.
104	
105	    Roots are every value read by a ``Return`` or ``Branch`` and *every*
106	    ``Call`` instruction (plus, transitively, its arguments): a call whose
107	    result is unused is still observable.  From each root the use-def graph
108	    -- instruction operands and phi incoming values -- is walked to a
109	    fixpoint, so a value only reachable from dead code or a closed phi
110	    cycle is absent from the result.
111	    """
112	    phi_by_dest: dict = {}
113	    operands_by_dest: dict = {}
114	    worklist: list = []
115	
116	    for block in func.blocks:
117	        for ins in block.instructions:
118	            operands_by_dest[id(ins.dest)] = _operands(ins)
119	            if isinstance(ins, Call):
120	                # The call itself is a root even if its result is unused:
121	                # reaching its dest below also pulls in its arguments.
122	                worklist.append(ins.dest)
123	        worklist.extend(_term_operands(block.terminator))
124	        for phi in block.phis:
125	            phi_by_dest[id(phi.dest)] = phi
126	
127	    live: set = set()
128	    while worklist:
129	        value = worklist.pop()
130	        if value is None or id(value) in live:
131	            continue
132	        live.add(id(value))
133	        phi = phi_by_dest.get(id(value))
134	        if phi is not None:
135	            worklist.extend(phi.entries.values())
136	        else:
137	            worklist.extend(operands_by_dest.get(id(value), ()))
138	    return live
139	
140	
141	def _eliminate_in_function(func: Function) -> Function:
142	    live = _live_definitions(func)
143	
144	    new_blocks = [Block(block.id) for block in func.blocks]
145	    block_map = dict(zip(func.blocks, new_blocks))
146	
147	    # Pre-create one fresh Temp for every surviving definition before
148	    # cloning anything: a phi in an earlier block (e.g. a loop header's
149	    # backedge entry) can reference an instruction defined in a later
150	    # block, and every retained use must resolve to the very same output
151	    # object.  Original ids are kept, so numbering holes from removed
152	    # definitions remain.
153	    value_map: dict = {
154	        id(param.temp): Temp(param.temp.id, param.temp.type)
155	        for param in func.params
156	    }
157	    for block in func.blocks:
158	        for phi in block.phis:
159	            if id(phi.dest) in live:
160	                value_map[id(phi.dest)] = Temp(phi.dest.id, phi.dest.type)
161	        for ins in block.instructions:
162	            if isinstance(ins, Call) or id(ins.dest) in live:
163	                value_map[id(ins.dest)] = Temp(
164	                    ins.dest.id, ins.dest.type
165	                )
166	
167	    def map_value(value):
168	        if value is None:
169	            return None
170	        mapped = value_map.get(id(value))
171	        if mapped is None:
172	            # Defensive: a referenced value with no surviving definition.
173	            # Never occurs for SSA IR produced by to_ssa, where every
174	            # operand of a live construct is itself live.
175	            mapped = Temp(value.id, value.type)
176	            value_map[id(value)] = mapped
177	        return mapped
178	
179	    for block, new_block in zip(func.blocks, new_blocks):
180	        for phi in block.phis:
181	            if id(phi.dest) not in live:
182	                continue
183	            entries = {
184	                block_map[pred]: map_value(value)
185	                for pred, value in sorted(
186	                    phi.entries.items(), key=lambda item: item[0].id
187	                )
188	            }
189	            new_block.phis.append(Phi(map_value(phi.dest), entries))
190	
191	        for ins in block.instructions:
192	            if not isinstance(ins, Call) and id(ins.dest) not in live:
193	                continue
194	            dest = map_value(ins.dest)
195	            if isinstance(ins, Const):
196	                clone = Const(dest, ins.value)
197	            elif isinstance(ins, Copy):
198	                clone = Copy(dest, map_value(ins.src))
199	            elif isinstance(ins, BinOp):
200	                clone = BinOp(
201	                    dest, ins.operator, map_value(ins.left),
202	                    map_value(ins.right), ins.kind, ins.type,
203	                )
204	            else:
205	                clone = Call(
206	                    dest, ins.name,
207	                    [map_value(arg) for arg in ins.args], ins.type,
208	                )
209	            new_block.instructions.append(clone)
210	
211	        term = block.terminator
212	        if isinstance(term, Return):
213	            new_block.terminator = Return(map_value(term.value))
214	        elif isinstance(term, Jump):
215	            new_block.terminator = Jump(block_map[term.target])
216	        elif isinstance(term, Branch):
217	            new_block.terminator = Branch(
218	                map_value(term.cond),
219	                block_map[term.true_target],
220	                block_map[term.false_target],
221	            )
222	
223	    new_params = [
224	        Parameter(
225	            param.name,
226	            param.slot,
227	            map_value(param.temp),
228	        )
229	        for param in func.params
230	    ]
231	
232	    return Function(
233	        func.name,
234	        new_params,
235	        func.ret_type,
236	        list(func.locals),
237	        new_blocks,
238	        block_map[func.entry],
239	        ssa=True,
240	    )
